the following:
 Order

Present miscellaneous appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicle Act is filed by appellant/claimant against the award dated 31/10/2014 passed by First Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Datia in Claim Case No. 18/2013 by which the appellant/claimant has been awarded a compensation of Rs. 38,066/- for the injuries sustained by him in road accident dated 24/12/2012; whereas, as regards liability of payment of compensation amount, respondent Smt.Kusum Gupta vs Virendra Sharma on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157654104/
1 No. 2,the Insurance Company has been exonerated from the liability of compensation and respondents No. 1 (owner cum driver) of the offending vehicle held liable for payment of compensation amount.
2 . T he necessary facts for the disposal of the present appeal in short are that on 24/12/2012 at about 4.30 am when appellant alongwith her relatives was going to Ratangarh Mata Mandir to seek Darshan on foot, it is alleged that as soon as they reached near village Jauniya, a Maruti Van bearing No. MP09BC7603 coming from the side of Indargarh, being run by its driver in rash and negligent manner, hit the appellant, due to which she sustained injuries in his left leg and other parts of the body.
Therefore, she preferred claim case before the claims Tribunal seeking a total compensation of Rs. 5,95,000/- from the respondents in different heads.
3 . Respondent No. 2 / Insurance Company appeared before the learned Tribunal and filed its written statement and denied each and every content made in the claim petition.

Insurance company has also taken the defence that at the time of accident, the driver of offending vehicle was not holding valid driving licence as he was holding learners driving licence and no person was with him as instructor, hence, insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation amount.
4. Respondent No. 1 also filed written statement denying the factum of accident by his vehicle.
He also denied that appellant sustained any grievous hurts and thereby permanent disability.

5 . Learned Claims Tribunal framed issues and recorded the evidence produced by the parties and after hearing both the parties partly allowed the claim application and awarded the sum of Rs.38,066/- and while exonerating the Insurance Company from liability of payment of compensation amount, fixed the liability of payment of compensation amount on respondent No. 1 with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of application. .
6. Shri Gupta, learned counsel representing the appellant contends that the injuries sustained by the appellant were grievous in nature.
The appellant sustained fracture in her left leg and she remained hospitalized for a long period.
She sustained permanent disability and after the accident not able to do the work which she used to prior to accident for her livelihood.
The Tribunal erred in disbelieving the disability caused to appellant whereas, as per disability certificate she sustained permanent disability to the extent of 25%.

The Tribunal has only awarded Rs 38,066/- towards hospital bill,
medical expenses, Special diet, pain and suffering and travelling expenses.
No amount under the head loss of earning has been awarded.
The amount awarded under other heads is on the lower side.
In view of the foregoing submissions, the enhancement of the compensation so awarded by the Tribunal has been prayed for.

Smt.Kusum Gupta vs Virendra Sharma on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157654104/
2 7.

It is further submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that learned Claims Tribunal erred in exonerating the Insurance Company from the liability and if this Court finds that Claims Tribunal did not err in exonerating the Insurance Company then also in light of catena of decisions of Apex Court, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation, which can be recovered from respondent No. 1 as if any breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy has been committed

,
then it is a matter between the owner/driver and the insurance company.
The claimants being third party should not be punished, therefore, burden lies on respondent No. 2 / insurance company to pay the compensation amount.
Hence, the finding with respect to the exoneration of the insurance company from its liability is liable to be set aside.
8. Per contra, the appeal is vehemently opposed by the counsel for respondent No. 2 / Insurance company.

Learned counsel for respondent No.2/Insurance Company did not opposed the quantum of compensation awarded by learned Tribunal and supported the award submitting that respondent No.2 / Insurance Company has rightly been exonerated and prayed for dismissal of appeal.

9. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
10.

As regards prayer of appellants/claimants regarding quantum of compensation, after having heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and on perusal of the pleadings and the evidence so adduced, in the opinion of this Court, considering the nature of injuries especially fracture sustained, treatment papers and its period, the mental pain and suffering and also the other heads,
the compensation as awarded by the Claims Tribunal is liable to be enhanced by Rs. 30,000/- in lump sum thereby making the total compensation Rs.38,066/- which shall be paid within two months from today.
11.

As regards appellant's second prayer to get compensation from Insurance Company with liberty to Insurance Company to recover the s ame from respondent No.1, since the vehicle was duly insured with Insurance Company, therefore, in light of Supreme Court decisions in the cases of Shivaraj Vs. Rajendra [(2018) 10 SCC 432], Manuara Khatun Vs. Rajesh Kumar Singh [2017 ACJ 1031] & Shamanna and another Vs. Divisional Manager, the Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. and others,[(2018) 9 SCC 650] wherein, it has been observed that in the case of breach of policy directions against the Insurance Company to pay the awarded sum to the claimants and then to recover the said sum from the insured be given by applying the principle of "pay and recover".

entities.text: Manuara Khatun Vs. Rajesh Kumar Singh [2017 ACJ 1031]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Shamanna and another Vs. Divisional Manager, the Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. and others,[(2018) 9 SCC 650]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Insurance Policy is a contract between the insured and the insurer and the insurer agrees to indemnify the insured against all the claims arising out of use of vehicle, however, such contract is subject to the conditions that the vehicle shall not be plied or driven contrary to the provisions of law as well as Insurance Policy.
Thus, it is clear that the insurer / Insurance Company can get away from its liability of indemnifying the insured by proving that the vehicle was being used contrary to the Insurance Policy.
However, the claimants are completely stranger to the contract between the insured and the insurer.

Once, the Insurance Company had agreed to indemnify the insured than it would be a dispute between the insured and the insurer as to whether the vehicle was being used contrary to the conditions of Insurance Policy or not?
But the claimants cannot be made to suffer because of inter se dispute between the insured and the insurer.

Once, the vehicle is insured, then the Insurance Company must satisfy the award and if it is found by the Claims Tribunal that the Smt.Kusum Gupta vs Virendra Sharma on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157654104/
3 vehicle was being used contrary to the conditions of Insurance Policy, then the right to recover the amount has been given to the Insurance Company without filing a separate suit against the insured.
12.

sentences.text: Thus, in view of aforesaid dictums, while allowing this appeal in part, in view of the forgoing discussions, the appellant is held entitled to receive the enhanced amount of Rs. 30,000/- in addition to the amount of compensation already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

The enhanced amount shall carry any interest as per the impugned award; however, the findings as recorded in impugned award regarding liability part is concerned, the findings of Tribunal to exonerate the respondent No.2 / Insurance Company from its liability to pay is hereby affirmed, however, in the light of principles laid down by Apex Court as above, it is directed that the Insurance Company shall pay the compensation to the appellant which may be recovered from the respondent No.1 / owner cum driver.
13. Resultantly, the impugned award is modified to the extent mentioned above.
14. This Misc. Appeal is disposed of accordingly.

(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE JPS/-
